question.text: An ATM NIFTY call option has theta = -15. If 5 days pass with no movement in NIFTY, what is the approximate per-unit premium loss from time decay (ignoring acceleration of theta near expiry)?

answer.text: Approximately Rs 75 per unit (15 × 5); the per-lot amount depends on the current exchange-specified NIFTY lot size
Rs 0 (no movement means no change in premium)

explanation.text: The Logic: Theta = -15 means the option loses Rs 15 per day per unit (approximately, assuming constant theta). Over 5 days: 15 × 5 = Rs 75 per unit. For a per-lot figure, multiply by the current exchange-specified lot size — NISM VIII notes that the NIFTY lot size is determined by the exchange and may change from time to time, so a hard-coded per-lot value (e.g., Rs 1,875 at lot size 25) can quickly become outdated. The Trap: Rs 15 is only one day's theta. Rs 375 multiplies incorrectly. Even with no underlying movement, an option loses value from time decay — "no movement" does not mean "no change in premium". Cross-Exam Context: Theta-impact calculations are tested in NISM VIII for equity derivatives. Per-lot conversion requires the current exchange-specified lot size.
